chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Reading and a piecemeal education
summary: Her education came as she went, through community work, including the East Bronx Community Council.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: more question about your childhood. Do you remember reading much as a child, and if so, the kinds of things that stick in your memory?

Oh, I was very much involved in my school work. When I left high school, I was quite studious, I was an honor student, I had an average of all A's, and I guess with some sort of encouragement and maybe with some funds I might have been able to go to college. But I didn't and we didn't--
You would have, there's no question about that. I'm sure from what I know of you.

Most of what I know now I've learned as I went. During the times when I was supposedly busy singing. In the theaters you always had time, so I did a lot of studying between shows, and then when I wouldn't be working steadily at a time, I would enroll in a class in one of the colleges here. I took different little courses, crash courses in dramatics, anything to enhance my career. And then of course when I got involved with the school system, then I picked up on a lot of things. I had the opportunity to attend different courses that they have in

conjunction with my duties, you know, and my involvement in the community here.

As you know, as part of my participation in the East Bronx Community Council, I received a scholarship to attend Rutgers, that's when I went down there and we took the saturation courses in community leadership.
So my education has been sort of piece-meal -- a little bit here, a little bit there.
Well, that's probably the best way.
And of course I had to learn a lot of things to enhance my own career, like study music in between times.
